# H-2A Paper agent documentation

> Grounded technical context for coding agents working on the empirical pipeline.

Start with the repository `AGENTS.md`, then run `python scripts/agent_docs.py snapshot --scope <target-path>`.
The machine-readable instruction and reviewed-source bundle is [`/grounding-manifest.json`](/grounding-manifest.json).

## Declared high-risk assumptions

- `ACCESS-001` (critical, repository data access) — Non-public NASS data and custom tabulations are unavailable by user instruction. Use publicly released NASS data; the implemented county-level work requires no farm-level nonparticipant frame or institutional-access application.
- `AUTH-001` (critical, repository) — Executable code, runners, locks, and machine checks outrank prose when sources disagree.
- `GROUND-001` (critical, agent documentation) — A source-region digest can be accepted only after the linked documentation context changes.
- `GEO-001` (critical, shared pipeline) — Persistent geographic identifiers are strings and county FIPS uses the 2010 vintage, including 46102 to 46113 harmonization.
- `EMPLOYER-001` (critical, H-2A worksite-business linkage) — The supported employer unit is the reviewed v2 worksite business linked with full FY2008--2024 identity evidence; the balanced tier is canonical, and alias-only individual masters are not counted as businesses.
- `PRED-001` (critical, prediction and shared panel) — The supported H-2A prediction is the static climate_norm_static_v1 model trained through 2011.
- `PANEL-001` (critical, shared panel) — The shared panel is design-neutral and excludes treatments, post indicators, design fixed effects, target clusters, and instruments.
- `OUTCOME-001` (critical, empirical designs) — The supported causal-outcome union contains fourteen outcomes, and each design's executable registry controls its subset, scaling, denominator, and sample rule.
- `DID-001` (critical, difference in differences) — The supported event study uses 2011 as its reference and clusters inference by CZ-by-AEWR-region.
- `IV-001` (critical, panel IV) — Panel IV retains the original moving-wage four-column design with deterministic county entropy weights and source year t-1. All branch stages and tests are R. The fixed-wage revision, later exploratory exercises, and simulated calibration draws were retired by explicit user instruction. estimation_spec.json is the sole model/outcome registry; controlled seasonal/composition column4 remains preferred. Preserve original donor support, prior behavior, twelve outcomes, reviewed business linkage, controls, equal weights, county/year FE and target-subregion CRV1. The farm-floor selection explicitly records the original all-domain Census source rows and refuses source-fingerprint drift; revising those choices is an empirical change. Recovered weights are not observed sampling errors; current FLS wage targets may induce mechanical relevance. The runner validates at stage09 and ends with the user-reauthorized stage10--11 Kitagawa decomposition diagnostic, which uses recovered weights as-is, fixes donor wages at their 2008--2010 real mean on a balanced donor set, and never replaces an instrument or selects a model.
- `MC-001` (critical, Mundlak-Chamberlain) — The supported MC version-4 default is a bounded linear-history OLS registry; randomization and bootstrap inference are disabled, and the scalar continuous CCV-HC3 mixture is an explicitly experimental comparator rather than a Lean-proved exact reference law.
- `WELFARE-001` (critical, narrow welfare) — The narrow welfare branch reports certification-space producer incidence for an anticipated real one-dollar AEWR increase, applies one frozen certified-hours elasticity to all shared-panel counties in its declared target years, and leaves paid-hours incidence as rho times the reported result.
- `BORDER-001` (critical, AEWR-border bounded redesign) — The standalone v6 border investigation retains all v5 benchmarks and evaluates four declared local redesigns. New members satisfy frozen agricultural screens and surviving-edge one-ring locality; direct current-real-AEWR, certifications/fixed2011 employment and county/component-year FE remain. Fixed weights/history and region-disjoint matching are labeled sensitivities. Pair inference is retained alongside shared-endpoint/spatial size/power and region deletion evidence; the nonstatutory 2009 wage is excluded from new wage diagnostics and FE-only noise calibration never uses it. No significance-based selection or empirical-adequacy claim follows from completed code. The separate statewide_design.json registry (stages 12-13) declares the 2025-10-02 statewide-AEWR state-border design before any post-policy outcome is parsed; its power uses only pre-period FE-only scale and actual statewide rates.
- `AEWR-001` (critical, AEWR source extraction and shared-panel consumers) — Canonical 2009 AEWR is null; application means are quarantined in explicitly nonstatutory fields. Annual references retain 1990--2025 independently of validation coverage. Dated FLS and occupation/skill tables retain job-cohort and competing-floor limitations. Shared outcomes survive wage missingness; stage04 alone reconstructs the contaminated historical comparator. Frozen 2009 OEWS loadings remain a distinct source.
- `WORKSITE-001` (critical, H-2A allocation calendar and point-geocoding producers) — Allocated certification position-days are capacity, not realized employment. Site dates and case fallback remain distinguishable; unreconciled cases are quarantined and county/month expansion conserves mass. Missing hours, unmatched counties and unacquired geocodes remain explicit. Outcome-weighted FLS references are timing diagnostics, and applicant locations do not supply a nonparticipant population.
- `REFORM-001` (critical, historical wage-reform investigation) — Historical wage-reform outputs are diagnostics, not a promoted causal elasticity. Cohort type and geography are fixed at baseline; absent certification is zero participation while wages stay missing. Observed 2009 application wages never assign statutory exposure, and old herder contracts are not grandfathered out of the wage increase.

## Grounding rule

A matching SHA-256 means the named source region has not changed since the linked page was reviewed. It does not independently prove the prose or empirical claim.
